decisive_items: ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, aVF, and V2 to V6
response.rationale: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy is supported by the classic triad of chest pain, ST-elevation and troponin rise with normal coronary arteries, plus confirmed apical ballooning on ventriculography. Pheochromocytoma is only suggested by an adrenal mass without catecholamine crisis features; acute MI is contradicted by normal coronaries.

rejected.why: Adrenal mass is an incidental finding; no hypertensive crisis or catecholamine-related symptoms to link it to the acute presentation.
Elevated troponin and ST-elevation are present, but normal coronary arteries on angiography directly contradict acute myocardial infarction.
